title: APOD: 2026 October 13 – Desert Stairway to Heaven
body: APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: This stairway in Chile brings you only a little bit closer to heaven. But ooh, the sky above it makes you wonder . For example, you may wonder about the dark lane of our own Milky Way galaxy rising behind the expansive Atacama Desert in Chile , the band of zodiacal light on the upper left, the green and red airglow just above the horizon, the star Spica in the zodiacal light stripe, and, at the very top on the right, the Small Magellanic Cloud galaxy. The Desert Staircase sculpture is in the foreground, and this image was timed to catch the picturesque peering perch just in front of the near- vertical Milky Way band . Upon close inspection of the horizon you can find, left to right, some Andes Mountains, the Licancabur volcano , and the town lights of San Pedro de Atacama . The featured wide-angle composite was captured in July 2025. Tomorrow's picture: open space
summary: "사막의 천국으로 향하는 계단"이라는 APOD(오늘의 천문 사진)는 칠레 아타카마 사막의 계단 조각상과 그 위로 펼쳐진 밤하늘을 보여줍니다. 이 사진에는 우리 은하수, 황도광, 에어글로우, 별 스피카, 그리고 소마젤란 은하 등 다양한 천문 현상이 담겨 있습니다. 지평선에는 안데스 산맥, 리칸카부르 화산, 그리고 산 페드로 데 아타카마 마을의 불빛이 보이며, 2025년 7월에 촬영되었습니다.

title: An Impact Structure With Legs
body: Editor's Note: Today's story is the answer to the October Puzzler . From above, the mere appearance of a curious geologic feature in Western Australia is enough to cause a fright. The aptly named Spider Crater, the product of a meteorite impact followed by hundreds of millions of years of erosion, sprawls across the landscape in the country’s Kimberley region . The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on the NASA-USGS Landsat 9 satellite captured this image of the crater on September 20, 2026. The full impact structure has an oval shape measuring about 13 kilometers by 11 kilometers (8 miles by 7 miles), with the spiderlike central portion measuring about 4 kilometers (2.5 miles) across. Geologists believe the unusual arachnoid pattern is the remnant of a central uplift , the raised portion of the crater floor that formed in the rebound of the initial impact shock. The light-colored “legs” are sandstone ridges that have endured while other rock layers in the impact zone have eroded away. For decades after the feature’s discovery, scientists struggled to weave a tale about its formation. Some proposed it had a volcanic past. But with some legwork in the field, geologists identified telltale signs of a past impact: fan-shaped fractures called shatter cones . These fractures form only when intense shock waves travel through rock, and they are ubiquitous in Spider Crater’s central dome. Scientists have subsequently performed lab analyses of shocked quartz and zircon crystals from the sandstone, which can help them reconstruct the angle of the meteorite’s impact. The date of the impact is uncertain, but estimates based on rocks in the region place it between about 900 million and 600 million years ago—making Spider Crater a creature of the late Precambrian. NASA Earth Observatory image by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey . Story by Lindsey Doermann . JPEG (23.76 MB)
summary: 서호주 킴벌리 지역에 위치한 스파이더 크레이터는 운석 충돌 후 수억 년간의 침식으로 형성된 지형이다. 이 충돌 구조는 13x11km 크기의 타원형이며, 중앙의 거미줄 같은 부분은 충돌 충격으로 융기된 중심부와 침식에 강한 사암 능선이 남은 것이다. 과학자들은 쇄석 원뿔과 충격받은 광물 결정 분석을 통해 이 거대한 구조가 약 9억에서 6억 년 전 운석 충돌로 만들어졌음을 밝혀냈다.

title: NASA’s SpaceX CRS-35 Mission to Launch Health Research
body: NASA experiments focused on human and plant health and drug-resistant organisms will travel to the International Space Station aboard SpaceX’s 35th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, advancing research that benefits life on Earth and future exploration. This research supports astronaut health during long-duration missions through four investigations from the agency’s Biological and Physical Sciences division, including 3D models of the human brain, a crop disease study, a faster way to assess astronaut health, and an analysis of antibiotic-resistant bacteria aboard the space station. Tiny brain models, big questions A new precision health investigation helps address a key question: What happens to the human brain in space? The experiment sends small, lab-grown models of the human brain to the orbiting laboratory for five weeks. Researchers compare tissue models that traveled to space with identical ones kept on Earth to determine how a short spaceflight affects the human brain at the cellular level. The effort could deepen our understanding of how the human brain responds to stress and help lay the groundwork for methods that counter risks to brain health that astronauts may face on future missions to the Moon and beyond. Disease-resistant crops for space A space crops investigation tests whether crop diseases develop faster and more severely in microgravity. The experiment compares molecular and structural changes between Earth-grown and space station-grown plants infected with a disease-causing fungus. The findings could guide plant breeding on Earth to produce disease-resistant crops and help minimize yield losses in future space agriculture systems. Space crops provide nutrition, increase dietary variety, and offer psychological benefits for astronauts during extended missions. They also absorb carbon dioxide, produce oxygen, and recycle water, which will become increasingly important as human missions extend farther from Earth. Analysis helps astronauts thrive The spacecraft also carries the first test of a compact microplate reader that arrived aboard the space station earlier this year. The Commercially Enabled Rapid Space Science initiative experiment tests the device’s ability to detect and measure certain biomarkers such as antibodies, antigens, and proteins. Use of the plate reader would allow scientists to analyze samples aboard the space station and obtain data quickly, rather than wait for the samples to return to Earth for analysis. Ultimately, the research aims to support the timely detection of infections and other health issues in astronauts while expanding science capabilities in remote exploration locations where resupply will be more difficult. Tracking antibiotic-resistant bacteria A precision health investigation returns for its fourth and final planned stay aboard the space station to study how antibiotic-resistant bacteria survive and evolve in microgravity. As part of the investigation, astronauts repeatedly sample surfaces throughout the space station to monitor for drug-resistant organisms. The work could help develop ways to protect astronauts against bacterial infections during long-duration missions. On Earth, the findings could provide insight into how superbugs develop from the overuse of antibiotics. To learn more about NASA’s biological and physical research in space, visit: https://science.nasa.gov/biological-physical/
summary: NASA의 SpaceX CRS-35 임무가 인간 및 식물 건강, 약물 내성 유기체에 초점을 맞춘 연구를 위해 국제우주정거장으로 발사됩니다. 이 임무는 3D 뇌 모델, 작물 질병 연구, 우주비행사 건강 신속 평가, 항생제 내성 박테리아 분석 등 네 가지 주요 조사를 포함합니다. 해당 연구는 지구상의 삶에 기여하고 장기 우주 임무 중 우주비행사의 건강을 지원하며 미래 우주 탐사를 발전시키는 것을 목표로 합니다.

title: APOD: 2026 October 12 – Jupiter and the Moons
body: APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: How many moons can you see? The best answer is five: four orbiting Jupiter and Luna orbiting Earth. This multi-moon picture was possible because Earth's Moon moved directly in front of Jupiter last week. The featured image is a series of exposures near alignment taken from Westchester , New York , USA . The sunlit crescent of Earth's Moon, on the lower left, is overexposed, while the Moon's night side, on the upper right, is faintly illuminated by Earthshine . Lined up nearly vertically above our Moon, listed from bottom to top, are Jupiter's bright Galilean satellites : Ganymede, Io, Callisto, and Europa. Callisto , Ganymede , and Io are larger than Earth's Moon, while Europa is only slightly smaller. NASA's robotic spacecraft Juno is currently orbiting Jupiter and has made close passes near three of these moons. Tomorrow's picture: stairway to heaven
summary: 지난주 지구의 달이 목성 바로 앞을 지나가면서 목성과 그 네 위성, 그리고 지구의 달이 함께 포착된 사진이 촬영되었습니다. 미국 뉴욕 웨스트체스터에서 찍힌 이 사진에는 지구의 달과 함께 목성의 갈릴레이 위성인 가니메데, 이오, 칼리스토, 유로파가 거의 수직으로 나란히 보입니다. 칼리스토, 가니메데, 이오는 지구의 달보다 크며, 현재 NASA의 주노 탐사선이 목성을 공전하며 이 위성들 중 세 곳에 근접 비행했습니다.

title: Antarctic Sea Ice Grows to Its 2026 Maximum
body: This story is an update to the Antarctic sea ice feature in our World of Change series tracking long-term change on Earth's surface through satellite imagery. Unlike the Arctic—an ocean basin surrounded by land—the Antarctic is a large continent surrounded by an ocean. Because of this geography, sea ice has more room to expand during the winter. However, that ice also stretches into warmer latitudes, leading to more melting in the summer. Antarctic sea ice usually peaks in September, around the end of the Southern Hemisphere’s winter, and retreats to a minimum in February. According to NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC), Antarctic sea ice in 2026 likely reached its annual maximum extent on September 14 (above). On that date, the ice covered an estimated 17.59 million square kilometers (6.79 million square miles), making it the third-lowest maximum on record. The maps below show the average concentration of Antarctic sea ice for the month of September (left) and the following February (right) from 1990 to 2026. Opaque white areas indicate the highest concentrations, and dark blue areas are open water. The images include only areas where ice concentration was at least 15 percent, a threshold scientists commonly use to count an area as ice-covered in satellite data. Scientists refer to the total area of these regions as the “sea ice extent.” From 1979 until 2014, total Antarctic sea ice increased by about 1 percent per decade. Whether the increase was a sign of meaningful change is uncertain because ice extents vary considerably from year to year around Antarctica. For three consecutive years, from 2012 to 2014, satellites observed new record highs for winter sea ice extent. These highs occurred while Arctic ice was in steep decline. The climb came to an end in 2015, and significant decreases in sea ice around Antarctica started to occur in 2016. There have since been years with small rebounds, but overall, Antarctic sea ice coverage has largely remained lower than normal. Both the record low minimum and record low maximum occurred in 2023. Scientists will continue to observe the area each year to find out if the decline is part of a long-term change or a statistical fluctuation. To determine sea ice extent, scientists rely on satellites with passive microwave sensors that measure the microwave energy Earth naturally emits. Sea ice emits more of this energy than open water, so it stands out in microwave images. Because microwaves pass through clouds, the satellites can observe sea ice regularly, regardless of weather. The record began in late 1978 with data collected by NASA’s Nimbus-7 , followed by Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) satellites starting in 1987, and by NASA’s Aqua satellite between 2002 and 2011. In 2025, scientists began using observations from the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency’s GCOM-W satellite . NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using data from the National Snow and Ice Data Center . JPEG (682.33 KB)
summary: 2026년 9월 14일, 남극 해빙은 최대 면적 1759만 제곱킬로미터를 기록했으나, 이는 역대 세 번째로 낮은 수치였습니다. 남극 해빙은 1979년부터 2014년까지 증가세를 보였으나, 2016년부터는 상당한 감소가 시작되어 2023년에는 역대 최저 최대치와 최소치를 기록했습니다. 과학자들은 위성 마이크로파 센서를 통해 해빙 변화를 관찰하며, 이러한 감소가 장기적인 변화인지 계속 주시하고 있습니다.

title: APOD: 2026 October 11 – Ice Fishing for Cosmic Neutrinos
body: APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: Scientists are melting holes in the bottom of the world. In fact, almost 100 holes melted near the South Pole are now being used as an astronomical observatory. Astronomers with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory lowered a long string knotted with basketball-sized light detectors into each vertical lake. The water in each hole soon refreezes. The detectors attached to the strings are sensitive to blue light emitted in the surrounding clear ice . Such light results from fast-moving secondary particles liberated when high-energy neutrinos emitted by powerful processes out in the universe collide with ice molecules. IceCube has now detected many illuminating neutrinos. Pictured in 2010, one of the last of IceCube's detector strings is lowered into the freezing abyss , making IceCube the largest neutrino detector ever created. In recognition of unprecedented discoveries , it was announced earlier this week that a founding leader of the IceCube Collaboration will be awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics . Tomorrow's picture: Moons Planet
summary: 남극 근처 아이스큐브 중성미자 관측소는 약 100개의 구멍을 녹여 농구공 크기의 광 검출기를 설치해 중성미자를 탐지합니다. 이 검출기는 우주에서 온 고에너지 중성미자가 얼음 분자와 충돌할 때 방출되는 푸른빛을 감지합니다. 아이스큐브는 현재까지 많은 중성미자를 탐지하며 가장 큰 중성미자 검출기로 자리매김했으며, 최근 그 선구적 발견으로 설립 리더 중 한 명이 노벨 물리학상을 수상할 예정입니다.

title: NASA to Conduct Flyover, Engage NFL Fans at MetLife Stadium
body: As part of the agency’s Inspiration Tour flyover, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will pilot one of three F-5 fighter jets to kick off the New York Jets vs. Cleveland Browns game in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sunday, Oct. 11. NASA team members will engage with fans at the agency’s Experience Zone, located at the Jets Tailgate Zone outside the stadium, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. EDT before the game. Fans can learn more about NASA’s return to the Moon under the agency’s Artemis dome, enjoy interactive games, and capture photos with a large, inflatable SLS (Space Launch System) rocket. Isaacman will be available for limited media interviews during the game. To arrange interviews, please contact Camille Gallo at: camille.m.gallo@nasa.gov or 202-531-8057. With stops across the nation, NASA’s Inspiration Tour convenes academic, industry, and public sector stakeholders to connect the agency with the people, technologies, and organizations that drive American leadership in space. The tour will culminate in MAX POWER, a public exposition of American air and space innovation, Saturday, Nov. 7, and Sunday, Nov. 8, on and near the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Held in honor of America’s historic 250th anniversary, the multi-day, family-friendly event will showcase the next-generation aircraft, spacecraft, autonomous vehicles, and technologies that will help define the future of transportation in air and space. For more information about MAX POWER and the agency’s missions, visit: https://www.nasa.gov/maxpower -end- Camille Gallo / Jessica Taveau Headquarters, Washington 202-358-1600 camille.m.gallo@nasa.gov / jessica.c.taveau@nasa.gov
summary: NASA는 10월 11일 뉴욕 제츠 대 클리블랜드 브라운스 NFL 경기 개막에 맞춰 F-5 전투기 편대 비행을 선보이고, 경기장 밖 '익스피리언스 존'에서 팬들과 만난다. NASA 관리자 제러드 아이작만이 직접 전투기를 조종하며, 팬들은 아르테미스 미션에 대해 배우고 대형 SLS 로켓과 사진을 찍는 등 다양한 체험을 할 수 있다. 이번 행사는 전미를 순회하는 NASA의 '인스피레이션 투어'의 일환으로, 11월에는 플로리다에서 항공우주 혁신 대중 박람회 'MAX POWER'로 마무리될 예정이다.

title: NASA Seeks US Industry Plans for Commercial Space Stations
body: NASA is advancing American leadership in space by taking the next step toward a future where commercial space stations lead the way in low Earth orbit. On Friday, the agency released its final Request for Proposals inviting industry to submit plans for the next generation of commercial space stations. “In alignment with the President’s National Space Policy, NASA is committed to maintaining a sustained American presence in low Earth orbit long after the International Space Station retires,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “We will continue to need a place to conduct research, develop technologies, train crews, and prepare for missions to the Moon and Mars. Commercial space stations may provide that capability while creating new opportunities for American industry and allowing NASA to concentrate more of our resources on the near-impossible missions ahead.” Building on the agency’s Ignition event earlier this year, NASA regularly has engaged with private industry to shape the agency’s future direction in low Earth orbit. This included publishing two Requests for Information in March to gather industry’s perspective on low Earth orbit destinations and transportation. The agency also published a draft Request for Proposals in July, followed by an industry day and one-on-one meetings that allowed interested companies to review and comment on the planned acquisition approach. “We’ve made it clear that NASA will never give up its presence in low Earth orbit,” said Isaacman. “Since Ignition, we have spent a lot of time listening to industry and working through what it will take to make this transition successful. The opportunity is significant, but the economics ultimately have to work. We want to see credible plans, strong technical execution, and companies prepared to invest in destinations that can serve NASA while developing additional customers and markets of their own.” Proposals are due Tuesday, Dec. 8, with contract awards expected in spring 2027. Under the solicitation, NASA outlines requirements for companies interested in designing, building, testing, certifying, and operating commercial low Earth orbit destinations capable of providing end-to-end destination and transportation services for human spaceflight use. NASA intends to award firm-fixed-price, multi-award, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contracts supporting development, certification, and services for continued low Earth orbit research and exploration. This will allow NASA to select two or more contractors through early development, followed by a competitive task order for final design, test, and evaluation, as well as certification and services from one or more contractors. Learn more about NASA’s missions on the agency’s website: https://www.nasa.gov -end- George Alderman / Joshua Finch Headquarters, Washington 202-358-1600 george.c.alderman@nasa.gov / joshua.a.finch@nasa.gov
summary: NASA는 국제우주정거장(ISS) 퇴역 후에도 저궤도에 미국의 존재감을 유지하기 위해 미국 산업계로부터 상업용 우주정거장 건설 계획을 요청했습니다. 이 계획은 연구, 기술 개발 및 승무원 훈련을 위한 시설을 제공할 차세대 상업용 우주정거장에 대한 제안서를 12월 8일까지 접수하며, 2027년 봄에 계약을 체결할 예정입니다. NASA는 여러 업체와 개발, 인증 및 서비스 제공을 위한 계약을 체결하여 지속적인 저궤도 연구 및 탐사를 지원할 계획입니다.
